I’m turning it into a real configuration boundary by exposing a profile-aware overload and moving the profile validation into that type.
The profile abstraction is real now instead of ornamental. I’m extending the tests to cover both the custom-profile path and the profile validation rules before I run the full suite.
I’m running compile and tests now. If the new profile validation exposed any rough edges, I’ll tighten them before finishing.

item.text:
Refactored [BalancedParentheses.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParentheses.java:1) so `BracketProfile` is now a real public configuration type instead of a private abstraction with one hardcoded instance. `isBalanced(CharSequence)` now delegates to `isBalanced(CharSequence, BracketProfile)`, and the profile owns its own construction and validation rules.

That makes the separation between delimiter definitions and stack validation meaningful. I added tests in [BalancedParenthesesTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParenthesesTest.java:1) for custom profiles and invalid profile definitions, while keeping the existing standard cases, `CharSequence` coverage, and null-input contract.

Verified with:
```sh
mkdir -p build/test-classes && javac -cp lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar -d build/test-classes BalancedParentheses.java BalancedParenthesesTest.java && java -jar lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar execute --class-path build/test-classes --scan-class-path
```
All 12 tests passed. I also sanity-checked `main` with `java -cp build/test-classes BalancedParentheses "{[()]}"`, which returned `true`.
